title: I Primi Verbi Irregolari: Andare, Fare, Volere
subtitle: Three high-frequency irregular verbs to get you talking about going, doing, and wanting.
objectives: Conjugate andare, fare and volere in the present tense
Use andare + a + infinitive for near-future plans
Use volere + infinitive to express wants

content.intro: Not every irregular verb waits until A2 — andare (to go), fare (to do/make) and volere (to want) are so common in everyday speech that you need them from the start.
content.explanation: These three don't follow the regular -are/-ire patterns you just learned, so their forms simply need memorizing. The reward is immediate: andare + a + infinitive lets you talk about near-future plans (Vado a mangiare, I'm going to eat), and volere + infinitive is the simplest way to express a wish (Voglio partire, I want to leave).

rules.heading: a) Andare + a + infinitive
rules.body: Expresses "going to [do something]": Vado a studiare. (I'm going to study.) The a is required even though English doesn't need an equivalent word here.

rules.heading: b) Fare in fixed expressions
rules.body: Fare is used for weather (Fa caldo, It's hot) and many activities that don't literally involve "making" anything: fare la spesa (to go grocery shopping), fare colazione (to have breakfast), fare una domanda (to ask a question).

rules.heading: c) Volere + infinitive
rules.body: Directly followed by an infinitive, no preposition needed: Voglio imparare l'italiano. (I want to learn Italian.)

examples.en: We want to go to the sea.

commonMistakes.why: Andare requires the preposition a before an infinitive — it can never be dropped.
Volere is followed directly by the infinitive, with no preposition — unlike andare.
Noi always needs its own form, andiamo, not the io form vado.

items.explanation: Io form of andare is vado.
Tu form of fare is fai.
Loro form of volere is vogliono.
Andare requires a before the infinitive.
Volere is followed directly by the infinitive, no preposition.
Andare + infinitive always needs a in between.
Volere never takes a before the infinitive.

summary: Andare, fare and volere are irregular and must be memorized: vado/vai/va/andiamo/andate/vanno, etc.
Andare + a + infinitive expresses near-future plans; the a is mandatory.
Volere + infinitive expresses a want, with no preposition needed.
